```markdown
# Roadmap — SEC filing-index ingestion

## Outcomes

Source: specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-spec.md. Background: specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-adr.md.
Choices made: Python 3.14 (`.python-version`).
Choices made: uv workspace of four packages (root `pyproject.toml`).

| # | Outcome | Spec | Track | Rank | Cost (estimate; basis) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| O1 | A baseline of archived quarterly filing indexes over a chosen range, original bytes kept | §3 R1; §2.1; §4.2 | A | 1 | ≈2 SEC requests per quarter (listing + index); range not yet chosen (§4.8); bytes per quarter measured by Stage 1 |
| O2 | Daily indexes ingested on an ongoing basis, catching up after missed runs | §3 R2; §4.2 | A | 2 | ≈1 index per business day plus listings, ≈250 files/year; bytes per file measured by Stage 1 |
| O3 | A canonical filing-index dataset in Parquet built from the ingested indexes | §3 R3; §4.4–4.6 | A | 3 | Parse time and peak memory per quarter measured by Stage 1 |
| O4 | The pipelines running on Azure (ADF, Container Apps Jobs, ADLS, Table Storage, Monitor) | §3 R4; §4.1; §4.9 | A | 4 | Azure spend unknown until the Stage 6 smoke run; spec §2.2 gives no cost guarantee |
| O5 | Backfill, daily and reconciliation sharing one downloader, parser and publisher | §3 R5; §4.1 | A | 5 | Developer time only |
| O6 | Reprocessing stored indexes after a parser change, with no new download | §3 R6; §4.3; §4.5 | A | 6 | Storage ≈ total raw bytes kept, from Stage 1's per-quarter figure × range |
| O7 | Periodic reconciliation of quarterly indexes, with changes recorded | §3 R7; §4.2; §4.4 | A | 7 | ≈2 requests per supported quarter per weekly run (§4.8) |
| O8 | All SEC traffic through one downloader on one request budget | §3 R8; §4.3 | A | 8 | 3 req/s target (§4.8) against the SEC's 10 req/s ceiling |
| O9 | Readers find current data through one versioned manifest and active pointer per quarter | §3 R9; §4.5–4.6 | A | 9 | Developer time only |
| O10 | Records leave the catalog only through hash-bound approval; failures never remove them | §3 R10; §4.4 | A | 10 | Partner time per gated quarter; frequency measured by Stage 5 |
| O11 | Stated defaults held in validated configuration, changed only through review | §3 R11; §4.8 | A | 11 | Developer time only |

Tracks: A — SEC filing-index ingestion (known progression).

## Stages

- [ ] Stage 1: One real quarter to Parquet
      Objective: Fetch one real archived quarterly index and one published daily index, keep their bytes, and parse both to the sec-index-v1 row contract locally.
      Outcomes: O1 (one quarter), O3 (one quarter, one daily file)
      Consumes: an SEC User-Agent identity from your partner (§4.8 `sec.user_agent`)
      Produces: a local fetch-and-parse path for one source file; specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-spec-stage-1-findings.md
      Exit: O1 — one quarter's index stored with its SHA-256 and byte count; O3 — Parquet rows for that quarter and the daily file, with row counts equal to their data lines; findings record bytes, rows, elapsed time, peak memory and request rate of the real run
      Leaves out: discovery, catch-up and range backfill → Stage 2; source & publication manifests → Stage 3; shared request budget and validated configuration → Stage 4; deployment → Stage 6; full validation suite and traceability → Stage 7; scheduling → Stage 8
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 2: Backfill range and daily catch-up
      Objective: Discover and ingest a configured quarter range and daily indexes since a handoff date through one shared code path, checkpointing per source file.
      Outcomes: O1, O2, O5
      Consumes: Stage 1's fetch-and-parse path and its findings
      Produces: per-source pending/failed/done state persisted across runs; overlap between baseline and daily resolved by key
      Exit: O1 — every quarter in a chosen range is ingested or reported as pending or quarantined with line and reason; O2 — a run after a simulated multi-quarter gap ingests every missed listed file and leaves failed ones pending; O5 — backfill and daily entry points call the same downloader and parser
      Leaves out: source & publication manifests → Stage 3; shared request budget → Stage 4; deployment → Stage 6; full validation suite → Stage 7; scheduling → Stage 8
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 3: Replay and versioned publication
      Objective: Picks up source & publication manifests: content-addressed raw and observation storage, per-quarter generations and a conditional active pointer.
      Outcomes: O6, O9
      Consumes: Stage 2's ingested sources and their state
      Produces: source/snapshot/processing manifest; per-quarter generations with manifest.json and an active pointer (§4.5)
      Exit: O6 — a parser-version bump rebuilds affected quarters from stored bytes with zero SEC requests and no duplicate logical records; O9 — a reader resolves each quarter only through its pointer and manifest file list, and a stale publisher's pointer write is refused
      Leaves out: Azure-backed storage and pointer → Stage 6; crash-injection tests → Stage 7
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 4: Shared SEC budget and configuration
      Objective: Route every SEC request through one leased collector with bounded retries, and validate configuration before any I/O.
      Outcomes: O8, O11
      Consumes: Stage 2's downloader
      Produces: a single-collector lease, retry and halt policy (§4.3, §5); typed configuration with §4.8 defaults
      Exit: O8 — concurrent backfill, daily and reconciliation runs never exceed one active issuer or the configured rate, retries included, and a 403 halts SEC access; O11 — each §5 configuration error is refused before any network request
      Leaves out: Azure Storage lease binding → Stage 6; lease-takeover fault tests → Stage 7
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 5: Reconciliation and withdrawal gate
      Objective: Refresh quarterly sources, publish safe changes, and gate closed-quarter removals on hash-bound approval.
      Outcomes: O7, O10
      Consumes: Stage 3's generations and pointer; Stage 4's request budget
      Produces: changes.parquet per generation; withdrawal approval records; `awaiting_approval` outcome
      Exit: O7 — a reconciliation run over real quarters records additions and updates, and skips unchanged hashes; O10 — a corrected fixture that removes keys leaves the prior generation active until an approval naming its hash, and open-quarter absence removes nothing
      Leaves out: weekly trigger → Stage 8; full validation suite → Stage 7
      ROUTING: writing-plans

- [ ] Stage 6: Azure deployment
      Objective: Picks up deployment: run the shared worker under ADF and Container Apps Jobs on ADLS and Table Storage, with managed identities and triggers disabled.
      Outcomes: O4
      Consumes: Stages 1–5 shipped; ADR and spec accepted with range, handoff date and environment recorded (§7 step 1)
      Produces: versioned infrastructure under infra/azure/; a pinned image digest; isolated-environment integration results
      Exit: O4 — in an isolated environment, ADF starts and polls a job to a terminal outcome, the Storage lease and conditional pointer work, and the §7 step 4–5 smoke and raw-only replay record byte counts, row counts, elapsed time, peak memory and request rate
      Leaves out: alerts and runbooks (traceability) → Stage 7; scheduling → Stage 8
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 7: Validation suite and traceability
      Objective: Picks up the full validation suite and traceability: §6 CI exit criteria, run reports, structured logs, alerts and runbooks.
      Outcomes: O4 (monitoring), O5–O10 (under fault injection)
      Consumes: Stage 6's deployed environment
      Produces: §6 CI suite; §4.7 run reports and alerts; docs/runbooks/ per §8
      Exit: every §6 CI criterion has a passing test; an injected failure of each §4.7 alert kind raises its alert; each §8 runbook is rehearsed once in the isolated environment
      Leaves out: scheduling → Stage 8
      ROUTING: writing-plans

- [ ] Stage 8: Baseline and scheduled operation
      Objective: Picks up scheduling: run the production backfill, daily catch-up and first reconciliation, then enable triggers.
      Outcomes: O1, O2, O7 (in production)
      Consumes: Stages 6–7 shipped; a reviewed image and configuration
      Produces: the release record (image, configuration, active generations)
      Exit: O1 — every requested quarter is published or recorded as an approved gap; O2 — daily trigger enabled after an accepted catch-up, and the next scheduled runs match their reports; O7 — weekly trigger enabled after one manual run with gated candidates resolved
      Leaves out: nothing
      ROUTING: writing-plans

## Stage-spec stamp

Every stage spec's Rollout note carries this line, which writing-plans then
copies verbatim into the stage plan's header:

> Roadmap: specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-spec-roadmap.md, Stage N — on plan
> completion, tick the stage and re-validate later stages against what shipped.

## Completion

When every stage is ticked, re-run the gap rubric over O1–O11 with evidence per
verdict (implementing stage and plan, Deviation notes, deferred items), and list
any spec §3 requirement that no outcome's `Spec` cell cites as unmet. Unmet
items exit as a new stage or as a deferral with a written why. Retire the
roadmap to specs/completed/ only after that audit.
```
